---
title: "1 · Committee"
---

The committee has 21 members: every materials model from the
[model comparison](../../comp_models/notes.qmd) plus three further models with
about 3–4.5 million parameters from other architecture families. MACE-OFF23 is
left out because it was trained on organic molecules and graphene is outside its
domain.

## Members

{{< include _committee_members.md >}}

"In PBE score" marks the 18 members whose training data are at the PBE or
PBE+U level. The selection score uses only these members. The three r²SCAN
members differ from the rest by functional as well as by model, so their spread
would partly measure the difference between functionals; their results are kept
and reported separately.

The evaluation time covers the whole candidate pool. For the MACE members it is
each model's own forward-pass time on the GPU, within shared batches; for
MatterSim, PET and GRACE it is CPU wall time; for DPA it is GPU wall time
including the throttle pauses. [Step 4](04_disagreement.qmd) has the details.

## New members

GRACE-1L-OAM (3,447,328 parameters) is a single-layer graph atomic cluster
expansion model from ICAMS, pre-trained on OMat24 and fine-tuned on sAlex and
MPtrj. It runs through `tensorpotential` 0.6.2.1 (TensorFlow) and is released
under the Academic Software License.

PET-OMat-XS v1.0.0 (4,487,962 parameters) is the extra-small point edge
transformer from the UPET package, trained on OMat24. PET-OAM is only released
in L and XL sizes, so the OMat24 model is the closest PBE-level option near
5 million parameters. It runs through `upet` 0.3.1.

DPA-3.1-3M (3,268,689 parameters) is the DeePMD-kit multi-task model trained on
the OpenLAM datasets. Its `Omat24` head was frozen with
`dp --pt freeze --model-branch Omat24` and runs through `deepmd-kit` 3.1.3.

SevenNet was considered but has no model near this size: SevenNet-Nano has
0.1 million parameters, SevenNet-l3i5 1.2 million, and the Omni and MF models
about 25 million.

## Environments

Each package has its own conda environment, created from conda-forge:

| Environment | Python | Model package | PyTorch or TensorFlow |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mace` | 3.12.15 | mace-torch 0.3.16 | PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 |
| `mattersim` | 3.13.17 | mattersim 1.2.1 | PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 |
| `upet` (new) | 3.12.15 | upet 0.3.1 | PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 |
| `deepmd` (new) | 3.12 | deepmd-kit 3.1.3 | PyTorch 2.10.0+cu128 |
| `grace` (new) | 3.12 | tensorpotential 0.6.2.1 | TensorFlow, with GPU memory growth enabled |

The new checkpoints are stored in `finetune_set/.models/` (ignored by git) and
their SHA-256 checksums are in `committee.json`. The MACE and MatterSim members
use the checkpoints in `comp_models/.models/`.

## Generators

One member from each class generated the configurations in steps 2 and 3:

| Class | Generator | Device | Share of configurations | Time per 100-atom force call |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| MACE | MACE-MPA-0 medium | GPU | 25 % | 23 ms |
| MatterSim | MatterSim v1.0.0-5M | GPU | 20 % | 28 ms |
| GRACE | GRACE-1L-OAM | GPU | 25 % | 7 ms |
| PET | PET-OMat-XS | CPU, 4 threads | 20 % | 36 ms |
| DPA | DPA-3.1-3M Omat24 | GPU | 10 % | 62 ms |

The shares follow speed, so that the generators finish at similar times. PET
runs on the CPU and at most three generators share the GPU, to keep the GPU load
moderate. The times are for a single 100-atom structure on an idle GPU.
